---
title: "I cannot start writing or stop revising"
last-reviewed: "2026-08-28"
---

## Find where the writing stalls

Try explaining the paragraph aloud. If you know what you want to say but can't get it onto the page, start with rough sentences. If you can't explain the point yet, check the question, evidence or argument first.

## Try this now

1. Write the reader's question and your answer in plain words.
2. Add the evidence, explain why it supports the answer and state its limits.
3. Give each planned paragraph a temporary heading describing its job.
4. Mark missing evidence or unresolved points so you can return to them.
5. Agree what this draft needs to show before review. Once it meets that standard, send it rather than reopening optional refinements.

## What to take when asking

Send the draft with its argument map, known gaps and one to three questions you'd like the reviewer to answer.

## Stop or change route

Polishing sentences won't settle an unresolved argument. Work on the argument first. When submission checks pass, reopen the design only if you've found a substantive problem.

## You are moving again when

You have a section ready for its intended review and know who will read it next.

Use the [argument map](../templates/synthesis-argument-map.qmd), [review cover note](../templates/supervisor-review-cover-note.qmd) and [good-enough rubric](../checklists/good-enough-rubric.qmd).
